title: Netflix Privacy Hardening Guide — Simplified Opt-Out Instructions (2026)
author: Compiled from Netflix Help Center (source-verified, retrieved 2026-09-13)

elements.text: Netflix Privacy Hardening Guide
Simplified Opt-Out & PII-Exposure Reduction Instructions

Source of truth: Netflix Help Center article “How to stop certain uses of your personal information” (help.netflix.com/en/node/100637) and the Netflix Privacy Statement (help.netflix.com/en/legal/privacy, Last Updated: April 10, 2026). Retrieved and verbatim-captured 2026-09-13; cross-checked by an independent verification pass.

This guide translates Netflix's own published controls into a prioritized, plain-language checklist, framed with standard data-protection security principles: data minimization (collect/retain only what's needed), least exposure (limit what third parties can link to you), and account-security hygiene (an attacker who owns your login owns every setting below — harden the account first).

Scope note: These are consumer self-service privacy controls Netflix documents publicly. This is not a bypass of any technical control and requires no special access — every action below is available to any signed-in Netflix account holder through the normal Account UI.
Priority Action Matrix
Do these in order. Each row is a self-contained action — skipping one does not block the others.

rows: Prevents an attacker from undoing every other setting below
Stops on-Netflix ad targeting based on your activity
Stops Netflix matching your email/phone to ad-platform profiles
Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
Opts out of CCPA-defined “sale/sharing” for ads + marketing
Device-level ad ID reset/limit (phone, TV, streaming box)
Breaks device-level ad tracking outside Netflix's own controls
Closes sessions you don't recognize; shrinks Netflix Household fingerprint surface
Removes titles from driving recommendations + visible activity
Request your data copy (verify what's held)
Confirms exactly what personal data exists before you restrict further
Delete phone number / unsubscribe marketing email+SMS
Stops marketing text/email; note password-reset SMS caveat below
Full account deletion (if leaving Netflix entirely)
Triggers Netflix's deletion process; irreversible after grace window

elements.text: Section 1 — Harden the Account First

Why this comes first: every privacy toggle below lives behind your Netflix login. Standard security practice (defense-in-depth) says secure the perimeter before configuring the controls inside it — otherwise account takeover silently reverts every choice you make.
1.1 Use a unique, strong password
• Password must be used ONLY for Netflix — credential reuse lets one breached site compromise this account.
• At least 8 characters; mix uppercase, lowercase, numbers, symbols; avoid personal info (name, birthday, address) [Source 11].
• Change it any time at netflix.com/password, or via a reset email/SMS.
1.2 Add a recovery phone number

• Account > Security > add a phone number, so you can recover access if you forget your password [Source 11]. (Tradeoff: this adds one more PII field Netflix holds — see Section 4 for the data-minimization counter-argument.)
1.3 Recognize phishing
• Netflix will NEVER ask for your card number, bank details, or password by text or email [Source 11][Source 12].
• Never pay through a third-party site linked from an email/text claiming to be Netflix.
• Forward suspicious emails to phishing@netflix.com; do not click links or reply [Source 12].
1.4 Audit and sign out devices regularly
• netflix.com/manageaccountaccess (“Manage Access & Devices”) shows devices active in the last 90 days [Source 3][Source 9].
• Sign out of anything you don't recognize, and always sign out before selling/returning a device [Source 11].
Section 2 — Stop Personalized Advertising Uses
2.1 Behavioral Advertising opt-out (per profile)
What it stops: ads selected based on your activity on unaffiliated third-party sites/apps over time [Source 1].
• Sign in on a web browser → select the profile → Account → “Privacy and data settings” → toggle “Behavioral Advertising” off [Source 1][Source 2].
• You will still see ads (if on an ad-supported/live-event tier) — they simply won't be behaviorally targeted [Source 1].
• Not offered on Kids profiles because Netflix states it does not run Behavioral Advertising there at all [Source 1][Source 3].
• Repeat per profile — this setting is NOT account-wide.
2.2 Matched Identifier Communications opt-out (per profile)
What it stops: Netflix using a hashed/pseudonymized version of your email or phone to match you on third-party ad platforms for marketing purposes [Source 1][Source 2].
• Same location: Account → profile → “Privacy and data settings” → toggle “Matched Identifier Communications” off [Source 1][Source 2].
• This is a separate switch from Behavioral Advertising — disabling one does not disable the other.
2.3 Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information
Some US state laws classify Netflix's ad/marketing identifier use as a “sale” or “sharing” of personal information [Source 2].
• Use the link in the footer of netflix.com, or go directly to netflix.com/dnsspi [Source 1][Source 2][Source 10].

• If your browser sends a Global Privacy Control (GPC) signal, Netflix states it honors that signal automatically where legally required [Source 2] — enabling GPC in a supporting browser/extension covers this without visiting the page manually.
• Caveat (Netflix's own wording): this does not retroactively undo previously “sold/shared” data, and does not stop all Behavioral Advertising by itself [Source 2] — pair it with 2.1.
2.4 Cookie preferences & “do not track” reality check
• Manage cookie categories at help.netflix.com/en/legal/privacy#cookies [Source 1][Source 2].

• Important: Netflix explicitly states it does “not currently respond to web browser ‘do not track’ signals” [Source 2] — the browser DNT header does nothing here; use the cookie preference center and GPC instead.
• Clearing browser storage (HTML5/IndexedDB/WebSQL) from your browser's own settings removes any similar-technology data Netflix may have stored client-side [Source 2].
2.5 Digital Advertising Alliance (DAA) industry opt-outs
These control OTHER companies' behavioral ads (not just Netflix's), for sites that participate in the DAA self-regulatory program [Source 1].
• United States — youradchoices.com [Source 1][Source 2].
• Europe — European Interactive Digital Advertising Alliance: youronlinechoices.com [Source 1][Source 2].
• Canada — Digital Advertising Alliance of Canada: youradchoices.ca [Source 1][Source 2].
2.6 Resettable device identifiers (phones, tablets, streaming devices)
Netflix may use a resettable device ID (e.g. Apple's IDFA, Google's Advertising ID) for marketing/ad delivery [Source 1][Source 2].
• This is controlled on the DEVICE, not in Netflix: look for “Privacy” or “Ads” in your device's OS settings and opt out / reset / limit ad tracking there [Source 1][Source 2].
• This choice is per-device — it does not carry over to a new phone, tablet, or streaming box [Source 1].
Section 3 — Reduce Device, Recommendation & Communication Exposure
3.1 Netflix Household device association
Netflix determines whether a device is part of your “Netflix Household” using IP address, device IDs, and account activity — explicitly NOT GPS/precise location [Source 6].

• There is no in-app toggle to stop this signal selectively — Netflix's own guidance is: “If you would like us to stop collecting information for this purpose on a particular Netflix device, please sign out from that device” [Source 1].
• Check/update Household from a TV, or review devices at netflix.com/manageaccountaccess and “Sign out of All Devices” [Source 6].
3.2 Limit what powers your recommendations
Netflix states recommendations use viewing history, ratings, similar-member patterns, and title metadata — and explicitly does NOT use demographic data (age/gender) for this purpose [Source 8].
• Hide a title: Account → Profiles → choose profile → Viewing activity → click the hide icon next to a title, or “Hide all” to clear all viewing history for that profile [Source 7].
• A hidden title stops counting toward recommendations (unless you watch it again) and is removed from Continue Watching; propagation across devices can take up to 24 hours [Source 7].
• This cannot be done from a Kids profile's Viewing activity page [Source 7].
3.3 Marketing email & text messages (SMS)
• Per-profile email/text preferences: Account → “Notification settings” for that profile [Source 1][Source 2].
• Quick unsubscribe: click “unsubscribe” in any marketing email, or reply STOP to a text [Source 2].

• Critical caveat: opting out of alerts/offers/surveys via those settings does NOT stop password-reset texts — Netflix states you will still receive a text if you request a password reset by SMS while a number is on file [Source 1]. To stop ALL texts, remove the phone number entirely: Account → Security → Mobile phone → Delete Phone Number [Source 1].
• Transactional messages (e.g., billing/account-critical notices) cannot be unsubscribed from regardless of channel [Source 2].
3.4 Push notifications
• Turn off in your mobile device's own notification settings, or via “Notification settings” for the relevant profile in the Account section [Source 1].
Section 4 — See, Correct, and Minimize What Netflix Holds
4.1 Get a copy of your data (verify before you restrict)
• Account owner: go to netflix.com/account/getmyinfo and follow the prompts; can take up to 30 days after verification [Source 3].
• Profile user (email added to a profile, not the account owner): email privacy@netflix.com — note the account owner IS notified of this request [Source 3].
4.2 Correct inaccurate data / object to processing
• Update directly in Account (email, payment method, phone number) [Source 9].
• For anything else, or to object/restrict/withdraw consent, contact privacy@netflix.com [Source 2].
4.3 Delete specific data vs. delete the account
• Viewing history → Section 3.2 above. Payment methods, phone number, profiles: see the linked Account sections [Source 4].

• Full account deletion: Account → Security → “Delete account” → complete Security Check → confirm. Deletion is deferred until the end of the current billing period if the membership is still active, and can be undone any time before that period ends [Source 13].

• If you only cancel (don't delete), Netflix's stated standard practice is to auto-delete the account 24 months after cancellation [Source 13] — cancel AND delete if you want the shorter, immediate path.
4.4 Retention — what Netflix actually commits to

Netflix's stated retention rule is deliberately general, not a fixed number of days: it retains personal information “as required or permitted by applicable laws and regulations… for billing or records purposes, and as otherwise necessary to fulfil the purposes described in the Privacy Statement” [Source 2][Source 4]. The one concrete number published is that the Access & Device Information view shows devices active in the last 90 days [Source 3][Source 9] — that is a display window, not a stated deletion timer for the underlying logs.
Section 5 — Honest Limits (What These Controls Do NOT Do)
A methodical privacy hardening pass should be explicit about residual exposure, not imply these toggles achieve zero data collection:
• Core account/billing/fraud-prevention data collection continues regardless of these settings — it is not optional while you hold an active subscription [Source 2].
• Opting out of “behavioral” ads does not stop ALL ads on ad-supported or live-event tiers — you get non-behavioral ads instead [Source 1].
• The Do Not Sell/Share opt-out does not retroactively claw back data already shared with third parties before you opted out [Source 2].

• Choosing an ad-supported plan is treated by Netflix as a “financial incentive” exchange under US state law — switching to a non-ad plan to reduce ad-based data use will likely raise the monthly price [Source 2].
• Resettable device ID and cookie opt-outs are local to that specific browser/device — they do not travel with your account to new hardware [Source 1][Source 2].

• No fixed universal retention period is published (Section 4.4) — you can request deletion, but Netflix retains discretion to keep data as long as legally permitted for billing, legal, or fraud-defense purposes [Source 2].
